newsitem.title: DENMARK: Danish bond prices hold, despite German doubts.
newsitem.headline: Danish bond prices hold, despite German doubts.

text.p: The Danish benchmark bond price held firm on Monday, despite worries about the likely size of Germany's budget deficit, due to go the German parliament on Thursday, dealers said.
At 8010 GMT the present benchmark eight percent state bond due 2006 traded at 110.95, up 0.01 basis points from Friday's close and yielding 6.33 percent.
The 10-year yield gap with Germany narrowed to 59 basis points, from 60 bp.
The crown was unchanged at 3.8070 to the mark. The six percent mortgage bond due 2026 fell 0.10 point to 89.00.

Dealers said that the imminent introduction of the seven percent 2007 bond as the new benchmark was likely to increase turnover as investors adjusted their portfolios. --Steve Weizman, Copenhagen newsroom, 45-33-969650
